topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture series on cancer etiology, and sets out the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Etiological origins of cancer across genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises through genetic mutations driven by the interplay of endogenous cellular errors, environmental mutagens, and population-level epidemiological differences.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and the Burkitt lymphoma paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and chromosomal translocations in Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how radiation, dietary toxins, and xenobiotically metabolized environmental compounds biochemically interact with cells to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic influences—such as chronic inflammatory stimuli, chemical promoters, and host developmental timing—create permissive microenvironments for clonal tumour outgrowth.

topics.label: Experimental and epidemiological methods for determining carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the laboratory assays, mutational signature profiling, animal models, and epidemiological cohorts used to assess and prove the carcinogenic potential of exposures.
